# Include files shipped with BlitzLLVM

Status: design, not implemented. Nothing in the compiler changes with this document.

## Why

Every program that reads the keyboard starts with its own `Const KEY_ESCAPE = 1, KEY_ENTER = 28, ...`. Thirteen of our
own samples and tests do this today, each with a slightly different set of names. The same goes for `WaitEvent` ids,
texture and brush flags, `EntityFX`, collision methods, `Graphics` modes and so on: the values are in the help, but
every program types them in again, and gets some of them wrong.

BlitzLLVM should ship these as include files in an `include/` directory of the installation, and give `Include` a
second form that looks there instead of next to the program.

## What the original does with `Include`

From the compiler source of Blitz3D (`compiler/parser.cpp`, the `INCLUDE` case; BlitzPlus uses the same compiler):

1. The token after `Include` must be a string constant. Anything else stops with *Expecting include filename*.
2. The quotes are removed and the rest goes through `GetFullPathName`, so it is relative to the working directory
   (the IDE sets that to the folder of the program).
3. If the file can't be opened, compiling stops with *Unable to open include file*.

There is no search path, and `BLITZPATH` plays no part. I could not run the 1.118 binary for this: Wine 9.0 aborts at
start-up in the cloud container (`free(): invalid pointer`, before any prefix exists), so these results come from the
source, not from the binary. Running the three test files below on a Windows machine with the original would confirm
them.

## Candidate syntaxes

| Form | Original 1.118 | Our compiler today | Tools that only know strings (old IDEs, IDEal, our formatter) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Include <keys.bb>` | *Expecting include filename* | *Unexpected '<', expected a file name in quotes* | Not a string: highlighting, `blitz-format` and the language server's include scan need changes |
| `Include "!keys.bb"` | *Unable to open include file*, unless a file `!keys.bb` exists next to the program | *Included file '!keys.bb' does not exist* | Works unchanged |
| `Include "<keys.bb>"` | *Unable to open include file*, always: `<` and `>` can't be in a Windows file name | *Included file '<keys.bb>' does not exist* | Works unchanged |

All three fail cleanly on the original, at compile time, with a message that points at the `Include` line. None of
them can silently pick up a wrong file on Windows except `"!..."`, because `!` is a legal character in a file name.

### Recommendation: `Include "<keys.bb>"`

* It reads like C's `#include <...>`, so its meaning is easy to guess.
* It stays a string, so every existing tokenizer, highlighter and formatter keeps working, including ours.
* `<` and `>` are not allowed in Windows file names, so the original can never open some other file by accident,
  and our compiler can tell the two forms apart without looking at the disk.
* On Linux and macOS `<` is a legal file name character, but a file literally named `<keys.bb>` is not something
  anyone has, and the form is decided by the text, not by what exists.

The rule: a string that starts with `<` and ends with `>` names a shipped include. Everything else keeps today's rules
exactly (relative to the including file, then to the main program).

`Include "!keys.bb"` would work just as well technically. Its downsides are that `!` doesn't say what it means and that
a real `!keys.bb` next to an old program would be taken by the original. The bare `Include <keys.bb>` is the nicest to
read, but costs changes in every tool and breaks highlighting in editors we don't control.

## Where the files are looked for

A shipped include is searched, in this order, and the first file found wins:

1. Every directory given with `-I <dir>` / `--include-dir <dir>`, in the order given. This lets a team keep its own
   shared library and use the same form for it.
2. `$BLITZLLVM_INCLUDE` (one directory, used instead of the one of the installation).
3. The directory of the installation, found like `userlibs` today:
   * `<prefix>/include` (Windows installer and zips, compiler in `<prefix>/bin` or `<prefix>/bin/<architecture>`),
   * `include` next to the compiler (build tree),
   * `<prefix>/share/blitzllvm/include` (Linux packages, Flatpak `/app/share/blitzllvm/include`).

Names inside `<...>` may have sub-directories (`<compat/blitzpointer.bb>`), use `/` or `\`, and are matched without
regard to case, like normal includes. `..` is refused so a name can't leave the include directory. A shipped include
that includes another shipped one uses the same form. A file is still only read once, whichever form named it.

Errors: *Shipped include '<keyz.bb>' does not exist (looked in: ...)*, listing the directories.

## Layout and packaging

| Where | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | `code_compiler/include/` (next to `code_compiler/userlibs/`) |
| Windows installer (per-user) and zips | `{app}\include\`, shared by the x64 and arm64 compilers |
| Linux packages / Flatpak | `share/blitzllvm/include/` |

CMake installs the directory with the compiler (`install(DIRECTORY ... DESTINATION include)` for the portable layout,
`share/blitzllvm/include` for the `system` component). The files are plain text and architecture independent. The
samples of #619 (`share/blitzllvm/samples`) can then use `Include "<keys.bb>"` instead of their own constants.

## The files

Names follow what Blitz programs already use (`KEY_ESCAPE`, `EVENT_GADGET`), upper case with a prefix per group.
The constants are ordinary `Const` declarations, so they show up in hover, completion and go-to-definition. Where a
table already exists (the scan codes on the Scan-Codes wiki page, the command list in `tests/suite/functions.txt`),
the file is generated from it so the two can't drift apart.

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `keys.bb` | `KEY_*` DirectInput scan codes for `KeyDown`/`KeyHit` (names from the Scan-Codes table: `KEY_ESCAPE`, `KEY_A`, `KEY_LEFT`, `KEY_KP_ENTER`), and `VKEY_*` SDL scan codes for `VKeyDown`/`VKeyHit` |
| `mouse.bb` | `MOUSE_LEFT`, `MOUSE_RIGHT`, `MOUSE_MIDDLE` (and the side buttons if the runtime reports them) |
| `joystick.bb` | `JOYTYPE_NONE/GAMEPAD/JOYSTICK` for `JoyType`, `JOYHAT_*` directions for `JoyHat` (-1, 0, 45, ... 315) |
| `graphics.bb` | `Graphics`/`Graphics3D` window modes and `GfxModeExists`-style values |
| `texture.bb` | `TEXTURE_*` flags of `LoadTexture`/`CreateTexture`/`CreateTextureEx` (including 3D 32768), `TextureBlend` modes, `TextureCoords` |
| `entity.bb` | `FX_*` for `EntityFX`/`BrushFX`, `BLEND_*` for `EntityBlend`, `PICK_*` for `EntityPickMode`, `COLLIDE_*` methods and responses, sprite view modes, `CameraClsMode`/`CameraProjMode` values, light types |
| `physics.bb` | Body kinds, shape kinds and flags of the physics commands |
| `audio.bb` | Flags of the sound and channel commands where there are any |
| `files.bb` | `FileType` results |
| `gui.bb` (BlitzPlus) | `EVENT_*` ids, gadget styles, `SetGadgetLayout` edges, `Notify`/`Proceed` results |
| `all.bb` | Includes all of the above |

### Gamepad buttons and axes

The runtime gives `JoyDown`/`JoyHit` the raw SDL joystick buttons, in the order the device reports them, like
DirectInput did. So `JOY_A`, `JOY_START` and the like would be wrong on many devices. Named gamepad buttons and axes
need the runtime to read gamepads through the SDL gamepad layout first (for example `GamepadDown(GAMEPAD_A)` and
`GamepadAxis(GAMEPAD_LEFT_X)`, keeping `JoyDown` as it is). That is a runtime feature of its own; `gamepad.bb` comes
with it, not with this change.

### Clashes with a program's own constants

A program that already declares `KEY_ESCAPE` and then includes `keys.bb` gets the usual *duplicate* error. That is
acceptable: including is opt-in, and the fix is to delete the program's own line. The compiler does not get special
rules for these constants.

## Compatibility includes

The pointer and threading design (#616) proposes a compatibility include for the memory functions of BlitzPointer and
friends. Those go to `include/compat/` (`Include "<compat/blitzpointer.bb>"`) once the language features they need
exist. Nothing in `compat/` is part of the first change.

## Tools

* **Compiler** (`code_compiler/source/parser_declarations.cpp`, `main.cpp`): the form check, the search list, `-I` and
  `--include-dir`, and the error message. `blitz-tidy` uses the same parser and gets it for free.
* **Language server** (`code_lsp`): `document::includes()` and the include graph resolve `<...>` through the same
  search list (`find_data("BLITZLLVM_INCLUDE", "include", true)`, already used for `userlibs`), so hover and
  go-to-definition open the shipped file. Completion inside `Include "<` lists the shipped files.
* **VS Code**: a `blitz.includeDirectories` setting passed as `-I` to `blitzcc` and to the language server. The
  Flatpak case needs nothing extra: compiler and server run inside it and see `/app/share/blitzllvm/include`.
* **blitz-format**: nothing, it only sees a string.

## Documentation

The wiki page *Language* gets a short section on the two forms of `Include`, with an `@difference` line, and a new page
*Include-Files* lists the shipped files and their constants (generated from the files, like the command tables).

## Tests

* A suite case per form: shipped include found, `-I` overrides it, missing shipped file, `..` refused, case and
  backslashes, the same file named by both forms is read once.
* Every shipped file compiles on its own and together (`all.bb`), so no two files declare the same name.
* `keys.bb` matches the scan code table of the runtime, and the generated files are up to date (like `wiki.py check`).
* The samples that define their own key constants switch to `Include "<keys.bb>"` in a separate PR.

## Open questions

1. Syntax: `Include "<keys.bb>"` (recommended), `Include "!keys.bb"`, or bare `Include <keys.bb>`?
2. Constant names: `KEY_ESCAPE` style as above, or with a `BB_`/`BL_` prefix to avoid clashes entirely?
3. Should `-I` directories also apply to the plain `Include "..."` form (C does not do this for `"..."` beyond the
   including directory), or only to `<...>`? This document says only `<...>`.
